theme: Trick-taking card games, built around tricks won by the highest-ranking card or trump.
decoy: Traditional adult card-table pastimes

members.title: Contract bridge
members.description: Fixed partnerships bid for a contract, then one hand is laid face up.

members.title: Whist
members.description: Georgian English partnership pastime with thirteen rounds and no bidding.

members.title: Euchre
members.description: Partners use a short deck topped by the two jacks of the same color.

members.title: Pinochle
members.description: A doubled deck of nines through aces, scoring melds and captured counters.

members.title: Skat
members.description: German three-hand pastime where a lone declarer takes on the other two.

members.title: Belote
members.description: French partnership favorite with a stripped deck of thirty-two.

members.title: Oh Hell
members.description: Hand sizes rise or fall each deal, and bids must be hit exactly.

members.title: Five Hundred
members.description: Australian favorite with a joker and a bidding table topping out at ten.

members.title: Sheepshead
members.description: Wisconsin favorite in which every queen and jack outranks the aces.

members.title: Jass
members.description: Swiss national pastime with a thirty-six-strong deck of acorns and bells.

intruders.title: Cribbage
intruders.description: Two rivals race pegs along a drilled wooden board toward 121.
intruders.why: No tricks are ever taken: the play phase is a running count to 31 and hands are scored for combinations. It belongs to the same traditional card-table world.

intruders.title: Gin rummy
intruders.description: Two opponents draw and discard to form sets and runs, then knock.
intruders.why: A draw-and-discard melding game; nothing is won round by round with a highest card. A classic two-hand pastime like Skat or Cribbage.

intruders.title: Canasta
intruders.description: Partners build big melds of seven from a double deck with jokers.
intruders.why: A rummy-family melding game with no tricks, though it is played in partnerships like Bridge.

theme: Net sports: a net divides the two sides, so opponents never share the same playing area.
decoy: Racket, paddle, and volleying sports

members.title: Tennis
members.description: Strung rackets, a fuzzy yellow sphere, and scoring in love, fifteen, and deuce.

members.title: Badminton
members.description: A feathered shuttlecock struck with light rackets, often from above head height.

members.title: Table tennis
members.description: A tiny celluloid sphere and rubber-faced paddles on a green or blue table.

members.title: Sepak takraw
members.description: Southeast Asian contest of kicking a rattan sphere with acrobatic scissor kicks.

members.title: Padel
members.description: Solid perforated paddles, glass walls, and underhand serves, usually in pairs.

members.title: Footvolley
members.description: Brazilian beach pastime of volleying with only feet, chest, and head.

members.title: Beach volleyball
members.description: Pairs dig, set, and spike barefoot on sand.

members.title: Pickleball
members.description: Perforated plastic sphere, solid paddles, and a no-volley kitchen zone.

members.title: Teqball
members.description: Hungarian invention that brings soccer touches to a curved table.

intruders.title: Squash
intruders.description: Strung rackets and a small rubber sphere that must be warmed up to bounce.
intruders.why: Both players share one enclosed court and hit against the front wall; there is no net. It shares rackets and scoring rallies with tennis and badminton.

intruders.title: Racquetball
intruders.description: Short strung rackets and a hollow rubber sphere rebounding off every surface.
intruders.why: Played in a shared four-wall court with no net, though it looks like a cousin of tennis and squash.

intruders.title: Jai alai
intruders.description: Curved wicker baskets hurl a hard sphere at blistering speed.
intruders.why: Opponents share the same fronton floor and play off the front wall; nothing divides them.

theme: Fully cooperative board games in which all players win or lose together against the game itself.
decoy: Modern thematic tabletop games for a group

members.title: Pandemic
members.description: Specialists race between cities to cure four spreading diseases.

members.title: Forbidden Island
members.description: Adventurers grab four treasures before a sinking island floods.

members.title: Hanabi
members.description: Build a fireworks display in order while seeing every hand except your own.

members.title: The Mind
members.description: Lay numbered cards in ascending order with no talking allowed.

members.title: Spirit Island
members.description: Island spirits drive off colonizing invaders with growing elemental powers.

members.title: Flash Point: Fire Rescue
members.description: Firefighters pull victims from a burning building before it collapses.

members.title: Mysterium
members.description: A ghost sends dreamlike picture clues to a team of psychic investigators.

members.title: Horrified
members.description: Villagers face classic movie monsters such as Dracula and the Mummy.

members.title: Arkham Horror
members.description: Investigators in a Lovecraftian town seal gates before an Ancient One wakes.

intruders.title: Dead of Winter
intruders.description: Survivors in a snowbound colony scavenge and weather crises during a zombie winter.
intruders.why: Each player has a secret personal objective and one may be a hidden betrayer, so the group does not simply win or lose together. It is marketed alongside co-op games.

intruders.title: Betrayal at House on the Hill
intruders.description: Explorers reveal the rooms of a haunted mansion tile by tile.
intruders.why: Partway through, the haunt usually turns one player into a traitor who plays against the rest. It opens as a co-op exploration game.

theme: Sports played with an oval, prolate-spheroid ball.
decoy: Football and rugby codes

members.title: American football
members.description: Eleven-a-side downs, forward passes, and touchdowns on a 100-yard field.

members.title: Canadian football
members.description: Twelve-a-side, three downs, and a 110-yard field with deep end zones.

members.title: Arena football
members.description: Indoor eight-a-side version on a 50-yard field with rebound nets.

members.title: Flag football
members.description: Non-contact version where pulling a strip from the carrier's belt ends the down.

members.title: Australian rules football
members.description: Eighteen-a-side on a huge cricket ground, with four posts at each end.

members.title: Rugby union
members.description: Fifteen-a-side with scrums, lineouts, and passing only backward.

members.title: Rugby league
members.description: Thirteen-a-side with six tackles per set before possession changes hands.

members.title: Rugby sevens
members.description: Fast seven-a-side version with short halves on a full-size pitch.

members.title: Touch rugby
members.description: Non-contact version in which a two-handed touch replaces the tackle.

intruders.title: Gaelic football
intruders.description: Irish fifteen-a-side code mixing kicking, hand-passing, and H-shaped goals.
intruders.why: Played with a round ball similar to a soccer ball. It shares its name and many traits with Australian rules and the other football codes.

intruders.title: Wheelchair rugby
intruders.description: Four-a-side full-contact code in reinforced chairs on a basketball court.
intruders.why: Played with a round ball developed from a volleyball, despite the rugby name.

theme: Shedding card games: the goal is to get rid of all of your cards.
decoy: Popular family and folk card games

members.title: President
members.description: Finishing order sets a social hierarchy, and ranks swap hands next deal.

members.title: Mau-Mau
members.description: Central European pastime of matching suit or rank on the discard pile.

members.title: Big Two
members.description: Cantonese climbing pastime where twos rank highest and poker combinations compete.

members.title: Durak
members.description: Russian pastime where attackers lead and a defender must beat each lead.

members.title: Speed
members.description: Two opponents slap down onto central piles simultaneously, with no turns at all.

members.title: Cheat
members.description: Discards go face down with a claimed rank, and anyone may challenge a lie.

members.title: Dou dizhu
members.description: Chinese three-hand pastime in which two peasants team up against a landlord.

members.title: Tien len
members.description: Vietnamese climbing pastime where the lowest three opens the deal.

intruders.title: War
intruders.description: Two halves of a deck are flipped against each other, the higher rank taking both.
intruders.why: The aim is to capture the whole deck, the opposite of emptying your hand. A classic family pastime like the rest.

intruders.title: Beggar-my-neighbour
intruders.description: Turned-over court ranks demand a tribute of several from the opponent's pile.
intruders.why: The goal is to win every card, not to shed them. A traditional folk pastime of the same register.

theme: Sports decided by judges' scores for execution and artistry, not by time, distance, height, or goals.
decoy: Acrobatic and spectacular Olympic events

members.title: Figure skating
members.description: Jumps, spins, and footwork performed on blades to music.

members.title: Artistic gymnastics
members.description: Vault, bars, beam, and floor routines of flips and holds.

members.title: Diving
members.description: Somersaults and twists from springboard or platform into a pool.

members.title: Aerial skiing
members.description: Skiers launch off steep kickers into multiple flips and twists.

members.title: Snowboard halfpipe
members.description: Riders link big spins and grabs above the lip of a U-shaped channel.

members.title: Artistic swimming
members.description: Synchronized routines of lifts and leg patterns performed in a pool.

members.title: Dressage
members.description: Horse and rider perform precise movements such as piaffe and passage.

members.title: Surfing
members.description: Riders carve turns and hit the lip on breaking ocean waves.

members.title: Breaking
members.description: B-boys and b-girls battle with power moves and freezes to a DJ's beats.

intruders.title: Slalom
intruders.description: Skiers carve down a steep course through tightly set gates.
intruders.why: Decided by the clock alone. It sits beside judged freestyle events on the winter program.

intruders.title: Pole vault
intruders.description: Athletes sprint and bend a fiberglass pole to fly over a high bar.
intruders.why: Decided by the height cleared, not by judges, though it looks as acrobatic as gymnastics.

theme: Video games presented from a first-person perspective, with the camera at the protagonist's eyes.
decoy: Landmark 3D action and shooter games

members.title: Half-Life
members.description: A theoretical physicist fights through a research facility after an experiment fails.

members.title: Portal
members.description: A test subject solves chambers with a device that links two surfaces.

members.title: BioShock
members.description: An underwater Art Deco city collapses into chaos after a genetic boom.

members.title: Mirror's Edge
members.description: A courier sprints and vaults across the rooftops of a sterile city.

members.title: Metroid Prime
members.description: A bounty hunter scans alien ruins on the planet Tallon IV.

members.title: Quake
members.description: Fast shooter of gothic dungeons, lightning guns, and rocket jumps.

members.title: Deus Ex
members.description: An augmented agent uncovers a global conspiracy in a near-future world.

members.title: System Shock
members.description: A hacker battles a rogue station AI named SHODAN.

members.title: Far Cry
members.description: A former special forces soldier battles mercenaries across a tropical archipelago.

members.title: Superhot
members.description: Enemies advance only when you do, in a stark red-and-white world.

intruders.title: Gears of War
intruders.description: Chainsaw-bayonet shooter where soldiers hold off a subterranean horde.
intruders.why: Uses a third-person, over-the-shoulder camera. It is a landmark shooter of the same era as Halo and Far Cry.

intruders.title: Max Payne
intruders.description: A grieving undercover agent uses slow-motion gunplay against a New York drug ring.
intruders.why: Played in third person from behind the character, despite being a genre-defining shooter.

theme: Consoles and handhelds manufactured by Sega.
decoy: Game hardware of the 1980s and 1990s

members.title: Master System
members.description: 8-bit system of the mid-1980s, long-lived and hugely popular in Brazil.

members.title: Mega Drive
members.description: 16-bit system sold on blast-processing ads and fast platformers.

members.title: Saturn
members.description: 32-bit system with twin CPUs, launched in Japan in 1994.

members.title: Dreamcast
members.description: Late-1990s system with a built-in modem and a memory unit with a screen.

members.title: Game Gear
members.description: Portable color system with a backlit screen, launched in 1990.

members.title: SG-1000
members.description: Early system released in Japan on the same day as the Famicom.

members.title: 32X
members.description: Mushroom-shaped add-on that slotted into the top of a 16-bit system.

members.title: Nomad
members.description: Portable version of a 16-bit system that ran its full library on the go.

intruders.title: TurboGrafx-16
intruders.description: Compact system with credit-card-sized game cards, called PC Engine in Japan.
intruders.why: Made by NEC with Hudson Soft. It was a direct rival of the Mega Drive in the same era.

intruders.title: Neo Geo
intruders.description: Arcade-grade system with huge, expensive cartridges, sold in the early 1990s.
intruders.why: Made by SNK. It shared the 16-bit era and arcade reputation of the Mega Drive.

theme: Winter competitions contested on ice rather than on snow.
decoy: Winter Olympic and cold-weather sports

members.title: Curling
members.description: Teams slide polished granite stones toward a target while sweeping ahead.

members.title: Bobsleigh
members.description: Crews of two or four push off and ride a steel-runnered sled down a banked track.

members.title: Luge
members.description: A slider lies feet-first on a small sled down a twisting chute.

members.title: Skeleton
members.description: A slider races headfirst and face-down on a small sled.

members.title: Bandy
members.description: Eleven-a-side stick sport with a small orange ball on a soccer-sized field.

members.title: Ringette
members.description: Canadian team sport using straight sticks to pass a rubber ring.

members.title: Broomball
members.description: Players in rubber-soled shoes swat a ball with broom-shaped sticks.

members.title: Speed skating
members.description: Racers in skinsuits circle a 400-meter oval in pairs.

intruders.title: Biathlon
intruders.description: Racers carry rifles and alternate skiing loops with target shooting.
intruders.why: Held on groomed snow trails. It shares the winter Olympic program with the rink and track events.

intruders.title: Snowboard cross
intruders.description: Riders race four to six abreast over jumps and banked turns.
intruders.why: Raced on a snow course, though it looks like the sliding and racing events.

intruders.title: Cross-country skiing
intruders.description: Racers glide over long trails using classic or skating technique.
intruders.why: Held on snow trails; its 'skating' technique is a ski stride, not skating on a rink.

theme: Pencil-and-paper logic puzzles invented in Japan.
decoy: Grid-based pencil puzzles with Japanese-style names or Nikoli popularity

members.title: Nonogram
members.description: Row and column number clues reveal a hidden pixel picture.

members.title: Slitherlink
members.description: Draw one closed loop so each number counts its surrounding edges.

members.title: Nurikabe
members.description: Shade cells to form a connected stream around numbered islands.

members.title: Hashiwokakero
members.description: Connect numbered islands with straight bridges, at most two between any pair.

members.title: Heyawake
members.description: Shade cells in walled rooms; no unshaded line may span three rooms.

members.title: Masyu
members.description: Draw a loop through black and white circles, turning or going straight on each.

members.title: Shikaku
members.description: Divide the grid into rectangles, each holding one number equal to its area.

members.title: KenKen
members.description: Fill a Latin square so caged groups hit targets via arithmetic.

intruders.title: Sudoku
intruders.description: Fill a nine-by-nine grid so every row, column, and box holds one to nine.
intruders.why: Devised by American Howard Garns as 'Number Place' for Dell Magazines in 1979; Nikoli later named and popularized it in Japan.

intruders.title: Kakuro
intruders.description: Fill white cells so each run sums to its clue, with no repeated digits.
intruders.why: Began as 'Cross Sums' in Dell puzzle magazines in North America in the mid-20th century; the Japanese name came later through Nikoli.

theme: Board and card games designed by Reiner Knizia.
decoy: Acclaimed strategy games built on auctions, tile-laying and hand management

members.title: Tigris & Euphrates
members.description: Build civilizations in ancient Mesopotamia, scored by your weakest color.

members.title: Lost Cities
members.description: Two rivals fund expeditions, risking losses on underfunded routes.

members.title: Ra
members.description: Bid sun tiles for Egyptian treasures across three epochs.

members.title: Modern Art
members.description: Gallery owners auction paintings under five different auction styles.

members.title: Samurai
members.description: Place tiles to capture Buddhas, rice fields, and helmets in feudal Japan.

members.title: Ingenious
members.description: Lay two-hex tiles to raise colored tracks, where your weakest color counts.

members.title: Battle Line
members.description: Win flags by forming poker-like troop formations along a line.

members.title: High Society
members.description: Bid for luxuries, but whoever ends with the least money is out.

members.title: Through the Desert
members.description: Lead camel caravans across a hexagonal desert toward oases.

members.title: Medici
members.description: Renaissance merchants fill ships with goods through a series of auctions.

intruders.title: El Grande
intruders.description: Nobles vie for control of the regions of medieval Spain.
intruders.why: Designed by Wolfgang Kramer and Richard Ulrich. It is a German-style classic of the same mid-1990s era.

intruders.title: For Sale
intruders.description: Bid on properties, then sell them for checks in a quick second phase.
intruders.why: Designed by Stefan Dorra. Its short double-auction structure feels very Knizia.

intruders.title: Acquire
intruders.description: Found and merge hotel chains while trading stock in them.
intruders.why: Designed by Sid Sackson in 1964; a tile-laying investment classic often grouped with Knizia's work.

theme: Video games developed by the British studio Rare.
decoy: Nintendo-era and Xbox-era console hits

members.title: GoldenEye 007
members.description: Split-screen spy shooter based on a Pierce Brosnan film.

members.title: Banjo-Kazooie
members.description: A bear and a bird collect jigsaw pieces across a witch's worlds.

members.title: Perfect Dark
members.description: Agent Joanna Dark battles a corporate and alien conspiracy.

members.title: Donkey Kong Country
members.description: Pre-rendered platformer with an ape and his young sidekick.

members.title: Conker's Bad Fur Day
members.description: A foul-mouthed red squirrel stumbles through adult-humor parodies.

members.title: Jet Force Gemini
members.description: Twin space heroes and a dog fight an insect army.

members.title: Battletoads
members.description: Brutally hard brawler starring three amphibian heroes.

members.title: Viva Pinata
members.description: Tend a garden to attract and breed papercraft animals.

members.title: Blast Corps
members.description: Demolish buildings in the path of a runaway nuclear carrier.

members.title: Sea of Thieves
members.description: Pirate crews sail a shared ocean hunting treasure.

intruders.title: Donkey Kong Country Returns
intruders.description: Revival of a classic ape platformer with two-player co-op.
intruders.why: Developed by Retro Studios, not Rare. It revives the Rare-made Donkey Kong Country series.

intruders.title: Star Fox 64
intruders.description: Arwing pilots fly on-rails missions with rumble support.
intruders.why: Developed in-house by Nintendo EAD. It is an N64 contemporary of Rare's biggest hits.

theme: Sports invented in the United States.
decoy: Popular modern sports with well-documented origins

members.title: Basketball
members.description: Five-a-side teams shoot through a raised hoop with a backboard.

members.title: Volleyball
members.description: Six-a-side teams volley over a high net, with three touches allowed.

members.title: Softball
members.description: Bat-and-ball game with a larger ball pitched underhand.

members.title: Ultimate
members.description: Seven-a-side flying-disc game with self-refereeing and end zones.

members.title: Snowboarding
members.description: Riders stand sideways on a single board down a slope.

members.title: Skateboarding
members.description: Riders perform ollies and kickflips on a wheeled deck.

members.title: Paintball
members.description: Teams tag each other with dye-filled capsules from compressed-air markers.

members.title: Wiffle ball
members.description: Backyard variant with a perforated plastic ball that curves wildly.

members.title: Kickball
members.description: Schoolyard game where a rubber ball is rolled to kickers who run bases.

intruders.title: Netball
intruders.description: Seven-a-side game of passing to shoot into a raised ring, without dribbling.
intruders.why: Developed in England in the 1890s from early basketball rules, so it looks like an American offshoot.

intruders.title: Ice hockey
intruders.description: Six-a-side teams on skates use sticks to drive a puck into a net.
intruders.why: Its organized form comes from Montreal, Canada, where the first recorded indoor game was played in 1875.

theme: Hardware whose software came on cartridges or plug-in cards rather than on optical discs.
decoy: Nintendo-era home and portable game hardware

members.title: Nintendo Entertainment System
members.description: Gray 8-bit box with a front-loading slot, launched in America in 1985.

members.title: Super Nintendo
members.description: 16-bit successor with Mode 7 scaling and a four-button face pad.

members.title: Nintendo 64
members.description: Three-pronged controller with an analog stick, launched in 1996.

members.title: Game Boy
members.description: Monochrome portable with a greenish screen and a falling-block bundle.

members.title: Game Boy Advance
members.description: Widescreen 32-bit portable released in 2001.

members.title: Nintendo DS
members.description: Dual-screen portable with a stylus-driven touchscreen.

members.title: Atari 2600
members.description: Woodgrain-front 1977 machine with a one-button joystick.

members.title: Atari Lynx
members.description: Wide 1989 portable with a color backlit screen, flippable for lefties.

members.title: Intellivision
members.description: Mattel's 1979 rival with a numeric keypad and overlay sheets.

members.title: ColecoVision
members.description: 1982 machine that brought near-arcade graphics into living rooms.

intruders.title: Nintendo GameCube
intruders.description: Compact cube-shaped 2001 machine with a carrying handle.
intruders.why: Used 8 cm optical mini-discs, Nintendo's first disc-based home system. It sits between the cartridge-based N64 and the Wii.

intruders.title: PlayStation Portable
intruders.description: Widescreen 2004 portable with strong 3D graphics and media playback.
intruders.why: Its games came on UMD optical discs. It looks like a portable peer of the DS and Game Boy Advance.

theme: Video games that first appeared as coin-operated arcade machines.
decoy: Iconic 1970s to 1990s video games

members.title: Pac-Man
members.description: A yellow circle eats dots in a maze while four ghosts give chase.

members.title: Galaga
members.description: A fighter ship shoots swooping insect-like aliens that can capture it.

members.title: Street Fighter II
members.description: One-on-one fighters from around the world, including Ryu and Chun-Li.

members.title: Mortal Kombat
members.description: Digitized fighters trade blows and perform infamous finishing moves.

members.title: Space Invaders
members.description: Rows of descending aliens are shot from a cannon behind shields.

members.title: Asteroids
members.description: A triangular ship blasts drifting space rocks into smaller pieces.

members.title: Frogger
members.description: Guide a frog across a busy road and a river of floating logs.

members.title: Dig Dug
members.description: A driller pumps up underground monsters until they burst.

members.title: Centipede
members.description: A shooter picks off a segmented bug winding down through mushrooms.

members.title: Q*bert
members.description: A long-nosed hopper changes the colors of cubes on a pyramid.

members.title: Defender
members.description: A ship protects humanoids from abductors over a scrolling planet.

intruders.title: Tetris
intruders.description: Falling four-square pieces must be fitted into complete rows.
intruders.why: Created by Alexey Pajitnov on an Elektronika 60 computer in 1984; arcade versions came later.

intruders.title: Super Mario Bros.
intruders.description: A plumber runs and jumps through the Mushroom Kingdom to rescue a princess.
intruders.why: Debuted on the Famicom in 1985; the arcade Vs. Super Mario Bros. followed in 1986.

theme: Winners of the Spiel des Jahres, Germany's main game-of-the-year award.
decoy: Acclaimed modern family board games

members.title: Catan
members.description: Settlers trade brick, wool, and ore to build roads on a hex island.

members.title: Carcassonne
members.description: Lay tiles to grow a medieval landscape and claim it with meeples.

members.title: Ticket to Ride
members.description: Collect colored train sets to claim rail routes across a map.

members.title: Dixit
members.description: Surreal illustrated cards are matched to a storyteller's hint.

members.title: Codenames
members.description: Two spymasters give one-word clues to find their agents in a grid.

members.title: Kingdomino
members.description: Draft domino-style tiles to build a five-by-five kingdom.

members.title: Azul
members.description: Draft colored tiles to decorate a palace wall in Portugal.

members.title: Dominion
members.description: Buy cards to improve a personal deck that is reshuffled as you go.

members.title: Camel Up
members.description: Bet on a chaotic camel race where runners stack on each other.

members.title: Cascadia
members.description: Draft habitat tiles and wildlife tokens of the Pacific Northwest.

members.title: Qwirkle
members.description: Match wooden blocks by color or shape in lines of up to six.

intruders.title: 7 Wonders
intruders.description: Draft cards over three ages to build an ancient civilization.
intruders.why: Won the 2011 Kennerspiel des Jahres, the separate connoisseur prize, not the main Spiel des Jahres.

intruders.title: Wingspan
intruders.description: Attract birds to wildlife preserves with an engine of food and eggs.
intruders.why: Won the 2019 Kennerspiel des Jahres, not the main Spiel des Jahres.

intruders.title: Splendor
intruders.description: Collect gem tokens to buy mines, merchants, and noble patrons.
intruders.why: Nominated for the 2014 Spiel des Jahres but lost to Camel Up.

theme: Chess openings that begin with 1.e4.
decoy: Named chess openings and defences

members.title: Sicilian Defence
members.description: Black answers with an asymmetrical flank pawn thrust, seeking sharp imbalance.

members.title: French Defence
members.description: Black builds a solid pawn chain but often struggles with a hemmed-in bishop.

members.title: Caro-Kann Defence
members.description: Black prepares a central counter with a quiet pawn step, keeping the bishop free.

members.title: Italian Game
members.description: White's bishop eyes the weak f7 square early, in one of the oldest lines.

members.title: Scotch Game
members.description: White strikes in the center on move three to open the position.

members.title: Scandinavian Defence
members.description: Black immediately challenges the center, often recapturing with the queen.

members.title: Pirc Defence
members.description: Black lets White build a big center, fianchettoing a bishop to undermine it.

members.title: Alekhine's Defence
members.description: Black's knight is chased around to provoke overextended White pawns.

members.title: King's Gambit
members.description: White offers a flank pawn on move two for rapid development and attack.

members.title: Petrov's Defence
members.description: Black mirrors White's knight sortie, counterattacking instead of defending.

members.title: Vienna Game
members.description: White develops the queen's knight on move two before committing the kingside.

intruders.title: English Opening
intruders.description: White fights for the center from the flank, often reaching reversed Sicilian lines.
intruders.why: Begins 1.c4. Its national name echoes the French, Italian, Scotch, and Scandinavian.

intruders.title: Dutch Defence
intruders.description: Black stakes a kingside claim with the f-pawn, aiming for an attack.
intruders.why: Arises after 1.d4 f5, though its national name fits beside the French and Scotch.

intruders.title: King's Indian Defence
intruders.description: Black fianchettoes and cedes the center before striking back with pawn breaks.
intruders.why: A defence to 1.d4 (typically 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6). Its name echoes the King's Gambit and its setup resembles the Pirc.

theme: Video games whose main playable protagonist is a woman or girl.
decoy: Acclaimed single-player adventure and action games

members.title: Tomb Raider
members.description: An archaeologist raids booby-trapped tombs with twin pistols.

members.title: Bayonetta
members.description: An immortal gunslinger battles angels using hair-summoned demons.

members.title: Beyond Good & Evil
members.description: A photojournalist exposes an alien conspiracy on a mining planet.

members.title: Horizon Zero Dawn
members.description: A hunter with a bow takes down robotic beasts in a post-apocalyptic world.

members.title: Celeste
members.description: A climber scales a mountain while facing anxiety, in precise pixel platforming.

members.title: Gris
members.description: A watercolor journey through grief where color returns to a faded world.

members.title: Heavenly Sword
members.description: A warrior wields a cursed blade to defend a doomed clan.

members.title: Shantae
members.description: A half-genie guards a seaside town with hair-whip attacks and transformations.

members.title: Ms. Pac-Man
members.description: A dot-eater navigates four new mazes, pursued by ghosts.

intruders.title: The Legend of Zelda
intruders.description: An adventurer explores an overworld and dungeons to recover Triforce pieces.
intruders.why: The hero is Link, a boy; Zelda is the princess he rescues. People often assume the title names the player character.

intruders.title: The Last of Us
intruders.description: A smuggler escorts a teenager across a fungus-ravaged America.
intruders.why: The player controls Joel for nearly the whole game; Ellie is playable only in one section.

theme: Video games titled after a character the player does not control.
decoy: Video games whose titles contain a character's name

members.title: Donkey Kong
members.description: A carpenter climbs girders past rolling barrels to reach the top.

members.title: Where in the World Is Carmen Sandiego?
members.description: A detective follows clues around the globe to track down a thief.

members.title: Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine
members.description: Falling pairs of colored beans are matched in fours to clear them.

members.title: Wario's Woods
members.description: Falling monsters and bombs are stacked and cleared inside a forest tree.

members.title: Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!!
members.description: A small boxer climbs the ranks against towering opponents.

members.title: Mario Is Missing!
members.description: A plumber's brother tours world cities returning stolen landmarks.

members.title: Bowser's Fury
members.description: A plumber roams a lake of islands while a giant monster rampages.

members.title: Hey You, Pikachu!
members.description: Speak into a microphone to befriend an electric mouse.

members.title: Catherine
members.description: A man pushes blocks up a collapsing tower in nightmares about fidelity.

intruders.title: Donkey Kong Jr.
intruders.description: A young ape climbs vines to free a caged parent.
intruders.why: The player controls Donkey Kong Jr. himself, rescuing his father from Mario. Its title looks just like Donkey Kong's.

intruders.title: Luigi's Mansion
intruders.description: A nervous plumber vacuums ghosts out of a haunted house.
intruders.why: The player controls Luigi, the character in the title.

intruders.title: Super Princess Peach
intruders.description: A royal uses mood-based powers to rescue a kidnapped plumber.
intruders.why: The player controls Peach herself, even though she is usually the one rescued.

theme: Games named after a word or phrase that players say out loud as part of play.
decoy: Classic children's, party, and family games

members.title: Uno
members.description: Match the discard by color or number, with skips, reverses, and wild draw fours.

members.title: Bingo
members.description: Numbers are drawn at random and marked off on a five-by-five sheet.

members.title: Snap
members.description: Two piles are turned over one at a time until a matching pair appears.

members.title: Go Fish
members.description: Request ranks from opponents to collect complete sets of four.

members.title: Marco Polo
members.description: A swimmer with closed eyes tries to tag others in a pool.

members.title: Simon Says
members.description: Follow a leader's commands, but only some of them, or be eliminated.

members.title: Mother May I?
members.description: Children creep toward a leader by permission, with giant or baby steps.

members.title: Duck, Duck, Goose
members.description: A child circles a seated ring, tapping heads before a chase.

members.title: I Spy
members.description: Guess the object someone has secretly chosen from its first letter.

members.title: Red Rover
members.description: Two lines hold hands while a runner tries to break through the other chain.

members.title: Rock paper scissors
members.description: Hand shapes thrown simultaneously, each beating one and losing to another.

members.title: Red Light, Green Light
members.description: Runners freeze whenever the lookout turns around, or go back to the start.

intruders.title: Crazy Eights
intruders.description: Match the discard by suit or rank, with eights acting as wild.
intruders.why: Nothing in its name is ever called out; it is nearly identical to Uno, where calling 'Uno' is a rule.

intruders.title: Hide-and-seek
intruders.description: One seeker counts with eyes closed while everyone else conceals themselves.
intruders.why: The name is never spoken during play (seekers call 'ready or not'). Same playground register as Marco Polo.

intruders.title: Musical chairs
intruders.description: Children circle a shrinking row of seats until the tune stops.
intruders.why: Nothing named in the title is called out; the cue is the music stopping.

theme: Competitions in which the lowest score wins.
decoy: Games and sports decided by adding up points or strokes

members.title: Golf
members.description: Clubs, fairways, bunkers, and greens across eighteen holes.

members.title: Hearts
members.description: Four hands dodge hearts and the queen of spades, unless someone shoots the moon.

members.title: 6 nimmt!
members.description: Numbered cards join four rows; the sixth in a row takes the pile of bullheads.

members.title: No Thanks!
members.description: Pay a chip to refuse a numbered card, or take it along with its chips.

members.title: Show jumping
members.description: Horse and rider tackle a course of colored fences and water jumps.

members.title: Eventing
members.description: Horse and rider combine dressage, cross-country, and fences over several days.

members.title: Skyjo
members.description: Flip and swap a hidden grid of numbered cards, some of them negative.

members.title: Disc golf
members.description: Players throw flying discs at chain-and-basket targets around a wooded course.

intruders.title: Spades
intruders.description: Partners bid how many rounds they will take, and spades are always trump.
intruders.why: The side with the highest total wins, usually by reaching 500. It shares its deck and structure with Hearts.

intruders.title: Decathlon
intruders.description: Ten track-and-field events over two days, converted with a points table.
intruders.why: The most points wins. It is a multi-discipline format like eventing.

intruders.title: Sushi Go!
intruders.description: Pass hands around the table drafting sushi, tempura, and pudding.
intruders.why: The most points wins. It is a quick modern card game like 6 nimmt! and No Thanks!.

theme: Commercial games that repackage an older traditional folk game under a brand name.
decoy: Classic mass-market family board and table games

members.title: Parcheesi
members.description: Race four pawns around a cross-shaped track to a central home.

members.title: Ludo
members.description: Four colored tokens race home, sent back to the start when landed on.

members.title: Sorry!
members.description: Draw from a deck to move pawns home, bumping rivals back to start.

members.title: Chutes and Ladders
members.description: Spin and move up a hundred squares, climbing or sliding along the way.

members.title: Battleship
members.description: Opponents call grid coordinates to sink each other's hidden fleets.

members.title: Yahtzee
members.description: Roll five dice up to three times to fill a scorecard of combinations.

members.title: Kalah
members.description: Sow seeds around a ring of pits, capturing into your store.

members.title: Pente
members.description: Place stones to make five in a row or capture pairs by bracketing them.

intruders.title: Candy Land
intruders.description: Draw colored cards to move along a sugary path to a candy castle.
intruders.why: An original 1940s design by Eleanor Abbott, not a version of an older folk game, though it is a simple race game like Chutes and Ladders.

intruders.title: The Game of Life
intruders.description: Spin a wheel to travel a road of careers, marriage, and retirement.
intruders.why: Descends from Milton Bradley's own 1860 design, The Checkered Game of Life, not from a folk game.

intruders.title: Guess Who?
intruders.description: Ask yes-or-no questions to identify an opponent's hidden face.
intruders.why: An original 1979 design by Theo and Ora Coster.

theme: Consoles able to run their direct predecessor's library natively from launch.
decoy: Successor game systems from Nintendo, Sony, Microsoft, and Atari

members.title: Game Boy Color
members.description: 1998 portable that added a color screen and an infrared port.

members.title: Nintendo 3DS
members.description: Portable with a glasses-free stereoscopic top screen.

members.title: Wii
members.description: Motion-sensing remote and nunchuk, with a slim white upright body.

members.title: Wii U
members.description: Tablet-style GamePad with its own second screen.

members.title: PlayStation 2
members.description: Black upright tower that doubled as a DVD deck.

members.title: Atari 7800
members.description: 1986 successor built around a sprite chip nicknamed MARIA.

members.title: PlayStation 5
members.description: Tall two-tone machine with a haptic DualSense controller.

members.title: Xbox Series X
members.description: Monolithic black upright box with a fast solid-state drive.

intruders.title: PlayStation 4
intruders.description: Slim angular box with a touchpad DualShock 4 controller.
intruders.why: Cannot run PS3 discs; the earlier library reached it only through streaming and remasters. Its siblings PS2 and PS5 do run their predecessors' games.

intruders.title: Nintendo Switch
intruders.description: Hybrid machine that docks to a TV or goes portable with Joy-Con.
intruders.why: Cannot play Wii U discs or 3DS cards, unlike the Wii U and 3DS before it.

theme: Impartial contests, in which every option open to one competitor is equally open to the other.
decoy: Two-player abstract games studied in combinatorial game theory

members.title: Nim
members.description: Take any number of counters from a single heap; taking the last decides it.

members.title: Kayles
members.description: Knock down one or two adjacent pins from a row.

members.title: Chomp
members.description: Bite a rectangle of chocolate; the poisoned corner square loses.

members.title: Sprouts
members.description: Join dots with curves, adding a new dot on each curve, until stuck.

members.title: Wythoff's game
members.description: Remove counters from one pile, or equal amounts from both of two piles.

members.title: Cram
members.description: Place dominoes on a checkerboard in either orientation until none fit.

members.title: Quarto
members.description: Sixteen pieces with four traits; your rival picks which one you place.

members.title: Sylver coinage
members.description: Name positive integers that are not sums of earlier choices; naming 1 loses.

members.title: Subtract a square
members.description: Remove a perfect-square number of counters from a heap.

intruders.title: Domineering
intruders.description: Place dominoes on a checkerboard, one side upright and the other lying flat.
intruders.why: Partizan: each player has a different set of legal moves. It is the partizan twin of Cram.

intruders.title: Hex
intruders.description: Claim cells on a rhombus of hexagons to link your two edges.
intruders.why: Partizan: each player places stones of their own color and connects their own pair of edges. It is a famous mathematician-designed abstract like Chomp or Sprouts.

intruders.title: Tic-tac-toe
intruders.description: Place marks on a three-by-three grid to get three in a row.
intruders.why: Partizan: one player can only place X and the other only O.

theme: Games available on the day their console first went on sale.
decoy: Flagship first-party mascot and showcase games

members.title: Wii Sports
members.description: Motion-controlled tennis, bowling, golf, baseball, and boxing.

members.title: Super Mario World
members.description: A plumber rides a green dinosaur across Dinosaur Land.

members.title: Super Mario 64
members.description: A plumber explores painting worlds inside a castle in full 3D.

members.title: Halo: Combat Evolved
members.description: A cyborg super-soldier fights alien forces on a ring-shaped world.

members.title: Resistance: Fall of Man
members.description: Alternate-history shooter where soldiers fight an alien Chimera invasion of Britain.

members.title: Nintendo Land
members.description: Theme-park collection of minigames built around a second screen.

members.title: Astro's Playroom
members.description: A small robot explores a machine's interior, showing off haptic feedback.

members.title: F-Zero
members.description: Futuristic hover-racing on flat tracks rendered with Mode 7 scaling.

members.title: Super Mario Land
members.description: A plumber travels through Sarasaland on a small monochrome screen.

intruders.title: Sonic the Hedgehog
intruders.description: A blue hedgehog speeds through loops to free animals from robots.
intruders.why: Released in 1991, years after the Mega Drive launched in Japan (1988) and North America (1989).

intruders.title: Crash Bandicoot
intruders.description: A marsupial spins through jungle levels, running into the screen.
intruders.why: Released in 1996, well after the PlayStation launched in 1994-95.

intruders.title: Super Mario Galaxy
intruders.description: A plumber leaps between tiny planets with their own gravity.
intruders.why: Released in November 2007, a year after the Wii launched.

theme: Characters who debuted in a game named for someone else and later headlined a game of their own.
decoy: Famous platform-game mascots

members.title: Mario
members.description: Mustached plumber in a red cap and blue overalls.

members.title: Wario
members.description: Greedy yellow-capped rival with a zigzag mustache and a garlic habit.

members.title: Yoshi
members.description: Green dinosaur who flutters and swallows enemies with a long tongue.

members.title: Knuckles
members.description: Red echidna who glides and climbs, guarding a giant emerald.

members.title: Tails
members.description: Two-tailed fox who flies by spinning his tails like a rotor.

members.title: Shadow the Hedgehog
members.description: Black-and-red hedgehog created as the Ultimate Life Form.

members.title: Tingle
members.description: Balloon-riding mapmaker in a green suit who believes he is a fairy.

members.title: Captain Toad
members.description: Mushroom-headed explorer with a headlamp and heavy backpack.

members.title: Diddy Kong
members.description: Red-capped young monkey who carries peanut popguns.

intruders.title: Kirby
intruders.description: Pink round puffball who inhales enemies to copy their powers.
intruders.why: Debuted as the star of his own game, Kirby's Dream Land (1992).

intruders.title: Rayman
intruders.description: Limbless hero whose hands and feet float free of his body.
intruders.why: Debuted as the star of his own game, Rayman (1995), rather than in someone else's.

theme: Games whose own title became part of the name of a genre.
decoy: Hugely influential genre-defining video games

members.title: Rogue
members.description: Descend a randomly generated ASCII dungeon with permanent death.

members.title: Doom
members.description: A space marine blasts demons through bases on the moons of Mars.

members.title: Dark Souls
members.description: Punishing dark fantasy with bonfire checkpoints and dropped souls on death.

members.title: Grand Theft Auto
members.description: Steal cars and take jobs from criminals across an open city.

members.title: Diablo
members.description: Click to slay hordes beneath a cursed town in search of loot.

members.title: Myst
members.description: Explore a silent island of pre-rendered puzzles and linking books.

members.title: Castlevania
members.description: A whip-wielding vampire hunter storms Dracula's castle.

members.title: Metroid
members.description: A bounty hunter explores the caverns of planet Zebes.

intruders.title: PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds
intruders.description: A hundred parachute onto an island and fight until one remains.
intruders.why: The 'battle royale' label comes from the 2000 Japanese film Battle Royale, not from this game, which popularized the format.

intruders.title: Wolfenstein 3D
intruders.description: An escaped prisoner of war shoots through castle corridors.
intruders.why: It pioneered the first-person shooter, but early imitators were called 'Doom clones', not after this game.
